packageRules.description: CI-MINUTE BUDGET (Oct 2026). Every Renovate PR runs full CI, and so does its merge, so one PR per package was about 450 PRs a month across the estate. All non-major updates now arrive together, in a window on the 1st-3rd of the month (wide enough that automerge PRs pass CI and merge inside it, because updateNotScheduled is false), in two PRs per repository split by merge policy: this one (reviewed) and 'non-major (automerge)'. Docker digest updates ride here too. Security fixes are not affected: vulnerabilityAlerts ignores schedule and grouping and opens at once.
Dev tooling churns constantly and cannot break production. Let it through on green CI.
A major bump is a migration, not an update. Always human-reviewed, and no PR (so no CI run) until it is ticked on the Dependency Dashboard.
Let a release sit long enough that someone else finds the regression first.

Non-major GitHub Actions bumps ride in the automerge group. helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests above converts tags to digests, so this is also what keeps those digests fresh. Action majors are not matched here: the major rule above keeps them human-reviewed, behind dashboard approval.

This estate's own reusable workflows are referenced at the moving @v1 tag, so a change ships by moving the tag (move-major-tag.yml) with no pull request anywhere. Renovate pinning them to digests, or chasing main, turned every change into a PR in every consuming repository, each running full CI. Callers still pinned to a SHA must be moved to @v1 once by hand: Renovate no longer touches them.
